title: blocking spec
description: episodes/<slug>/<EPID>/_context/blocking.json — the single geometry authority, authored at 04d. Both the clip prompt (04f/04f3) and the frame-0 still (04f2) are projections of this file and never re-decide its fields. Gates parse these fields rather than regexing prose.

clips.description: Keyed by clip id (SC01, SC02, ...). Clip ids are flat and sequential.

movement.description: Decided HERE, not at the prompt stage. A locked camera over a settled character reads as a dead freeze-frame; 'locked' is a deliberate choice that must be stated, not a default arrived at by omission.

anchors.description: Ordered actions. The clip prompt walks these in order; 05a's beat-adherence check names them.

end_state.description: Feeds the NEXT clip's continuity check (LTXV-S004).

frame0.description: 'rest' (pre-beat) is the default. 'peak' is a deliberate cold-open/reveal exception and pairs with a non-closed mouth state.

facing.description: Described relative to the CAMERA, never relative to another character. Camera-relative facing is what disqualifies bench/podium/head-of-table geometry that puts a speaker's back to the lens.

expression.description: Its own field, never folded into pose — an emotional read buried in a posture string cannot be independently reviewed, and this is what the clip QA performance column checks against.

mouth.description: Explicit for EVERY character, not just the speaker. Defaults to 'closed'; override only for a genuine frame0:peak scene.

hands.description: An empty hand is stated as empty. A prop that will be 'placed' during the clip is already at its placed resting_state — a prop seeded mid-placement lingers or duplicates in the render.

cue.description: Wardrobe or identity tag carried into both prompts.

visible.description: Only characters marked true are drawn in frame. An off-screen speaker is never rendered.

name.description: Concrete and specific — 'a small stuffed toy rabbit', never 'a small toy'. Reused verbatim every time the object recurs.

detail.description: The ONE permanent identifying visual mark, e.g. 'one flat dent beneath the handle'. Restated verbatim in every still and clip prompt for the whole episode — without it the model has nothing to be consistent with and the prop quietly becomes a different object scene to scene.
